definition_en: costing a lot of money, or causing a high cost

scene: 商店橱窗里摆着一辆标价很高的山地车，孩子看了价格吐舌头。This bike is too expensive for us.

senses.title: A high price
senses.example: This bike is too expensive for us.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自行车对我们来说太贵了。
senses.why: Expensive comes from expense, 'money paid out'; the adjective says that something takes a large amount out of your purse.

senses.title: A costly sacrifice
senses.definition: involving a high cost or sacrifice
senses.example: The mistake was expensive for the company.

senses.why: The same 'large amount paid out' idea applies to costs that are not money in a shop, such as time, effort or a bad mistake.

definition_en: to move downward, to drop to the ground, or to become less
core_image: 秋天的树下，黄叶一片片落下来，铺满地面
scene: 秋天的树下，黄叶一片片落下来，铺满地面。The leaves fall in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 fall 是「落下」（第 01 个义项）；句意是秋天树叶落下。

senses.title: To move downward
senses.example: The leaves fall in autumn.
senses.why: Old English feallan meant to drop down, and the same word still describes anything moving downward under its own weight.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 feallan 意为「向下掉」，同一个词至今描述任何在自身重量下向下移动的东西。

senses.title: To drop to the ground
senses.example: Be careful not to fall on the ice.
senses.why: The downward movement is applied to a whole person, so the verb names losing your balance and reaching the ground.
senses.whyCN: 把向下的移动用在整个人身上，这个词就表示失去平衡、倒在地上。

senses.title: To become less
senses.example: Prices fall in winter.
senses.why: Because a lower number is pictured as a lower position, the same verb describes amounts and levels going down.
senses.whyCN: 因为较低的数字被想象成较低的位置，同一个动词也描述数量和水平下降。

senses.title: To pass into a state
senses.example: He fell asleep on the sofa.
senses.why: English uses fall with adjectives to picture a change of state as a drop into it, as in fall asleep or fall ill.
senses.whyCN: 英语让 fall 与形容词连用，把状态的变化想象成跌入其中，如 fall asleep、fall ill。

definition_en: a group of parents and children, all related people, or a group in biology
core_image: 晚饭桌边一家人围坐，老人、父母和孩子都在
scene: 晚饭桌边一家人围坐，老人、父母和孩子都在。My family has five people.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我家有五口人。

senses.title: Parents and children
senses.definitionCN: 父母与子女组成的一家
senses.example: My family has five people.
senses.why: Latin familia meant the whole household, including servants; English narrowed it to the parents and children who live together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 familia 指包括仆人在内的整个家庭；英语把它收窄为一起生活的父母与子女。

senses.title: The whole clan
senses.definition: all the people related to one another
senses.example: The whole family came to the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 全家族的人都来参加婚礼。
senses.why: The older household sense widened again to the whole line of relatives, so family can name a clan across generations.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「家庭」义又扩展到所有亲属，因此 family 可以指跨世代的整个家族。

senses.title: The children of a couple
senses.example: They want a large family.
senses.why: Because the children are the growing part of a household, family is often used for the children alone, as in a large family.
senses.whyCN: 因为孩子是家庭中不断增添的部分，family 常单独指孩子，如 a large family。

senses.title: A group in biology
senses.definition: a group of related plants or animals
senses.example: The cat belongs to the cat family.
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the word for a group of related species, keeping the picture of one household of living things.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借这个词指一群亲缘相近的物种，保留了「同一家」的画面。

definition_en: a machine or hand tool that moves air, or a person who admires someone

senses.title: A machine for air
senses.example: Please turn on the fan.
senses.why: Fan for moving air comes from Latin vannus, a winnowing basket that separated grain from chaff in the wind.
senses.whyCN: 表示送风的风扇来自拉丁语 vannus，即扬谷用的簸箕，靠风把谷粒与谷壳分开。

senses.title: A hand tool for cooling
senses.example: She waved a paper fan.
senses.why: The same Latin word named the basket waved to make a breeze, and English used it for the hand tool that does the same job.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词指用来扇起风的簸箕，英语就用它指做同样事情的手持扇子。

senses.title: An eager supporter
senses.definition: a person who admires a sport or star
senses.definitionCN: 热爱某项运动或明星的人
senses.example: He is a football fan.
senses.why: This fan is short for fanatic, from Latin fanaticus, 'belonging to a temple'; its heated devotion became the modern sense of an eager supporter.
senses.whyCN: 这个 fan 是 fanatic 的缩写，源自拉丁语 fanaticus「属于神庙的」；那种狂热的投入变成了现代「热心支持者」的意思。

definition_en: land used for crops or animals, a place that raises animals, or to work such land
core_image: 清晨的田地里，成排的作物延伸到远处，旁边是红色的谷仓
scene: 清晨的田地里，成排的作物延伸到远处，旁边是红色的谷仓。They live on a farm in the country.
sceneCN: 这里 farm 是「农场」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们住在乡下的农场。

senses.title: Land for crops
senses.definition: land used for crops or animals
senses.definitionCN: 种庄稼或养牲畜的土地
senses.example: They live on a farm in the country.
senses.why: Farm first meant a fixed rent paid for land; the land held on such a lease took the name, and then any worked holding did.
senses.whyCN: farm 最初指为土地支付的固定租金；以这种租约持有的土地沿用了这个词，后来任何耕作的地块都这么叫。

senses.title: A place for raising animals
senses.definition: a place where animals are raised
senses.example: The fish farm raises trout.
senses.why: The worked holding was later applied to places that raise one kind of animal, such as a fish farm or a pig farm.
senses.whyCN: 「经营的地块」后来也用于专门饲养一种动物的地方，如养鱼场、养猪场。

senses.title: To work the land
senses.example: My uncle farms the land near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔耕种河边的那片地。
senses.why: English turned the noun into a verb, so to farm is to do the work that a farm exists for.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个名词用作动词，to farm 就是做农场该做的事。

definition_en: a person who works on a farm, owns one, or raises animals
core_image: 农夫戴着草帽在田里弯腰除草，手上沾着泥土
scene: 农夫戴着草帽在田里弯腰除草，手上沾着泥土。The farmer works in the field all day.
sceneCN: 这里 farmer 是「农民」（第 01 个义项）；句意是农民整天在地里干活。

senses.title: A farm worker
senses.definition: a person who works on a farm
senses.example: The farmer works in the field all day.
senses.why: Farmer is farm plus -er, 'one who works the land'; the ending marks the person from the work, as with teacher or driver.
senses.whyCN: farmer 是 farm 加 -er，即「种地的人」；这个后缀由工作指出人，正如 teacher、driver。

senses.title: A farm owner
senses.definition: a person who owns or runs a farm
senses.example: The farmer owns the land and the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 这位农场主拥有土地和谷仓。
senses.why: Because the person who works the land often also holds it, the same word covers the owner or manager of the farm.
senses.whyCN: 因为种地的人往往也持有土地，同一个词也指农场的主人或经营者。

senses.title: A raiser of one animal
senses.definition: a person who raises one kind of animal
senses.definitionCN: 专门饲养一种动物的人
senses.example: Her uncle is a pig farmer.
senses.why: English compounds farmer with the animal or crop, naming the person by what he raises, as in pig farmer or dairy farmer.
senses.whyCN: 英语让 farmer 与动物或作物组合，用所养的东西来指人，如 pig farmer、dairy farmer。

definition_en: moving or happening quickly, or done at high speed
core_image: 跑道上一个男孩冲刺，风把衣服吹得贴在身上
scene: 跑道上一个男孩冲刺，风把衣服吹得贴在身上。He is a fast runner.
sceneCN: 这里 fast 是「快的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他跑得很快。

senses.title: Moving quickly
senses.example: He is a fast runner.
senses.why: Old English fæst meant firm or fixed; a runner who holds firmly to the ground could go at speed, and 'firm' turned into 'quick'.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fæst 意为「牢固、固定」；跑者稳稳踏地才能跑得快，「牢固」由此转成「迅速」。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.example: She is a fast learner.
senses.why: The same speed sense is applied to the mind: a person who takes things in quickly is called fast, as in a fast learner.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「快」的意思用在头脑上：接受得快的人就叫 fast，如 a fast learner。

senses.title: At high speed
senses.example: The car runs fast on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速路上跑得很快。
senses.why: English uses the same form as an adverb, so fast describes the speed of an action without adding -ly.
senses.whyCN: 英语直接用同一形式作副词，因此 fast 不加 -ly 就能描述动作的速度。

core_image: 一只圆滚滚的橘猫趴在沙发上，肚子摊开
scene: 一只圆滚滚的橘猫趴在沙发上，肚子摊开。The cat is very fat.
sceneCN: 这里 fat 是「脂肪」（第 01 个义项）；句意是脂肪太多不健康。

senses.title: The oily substance
senses.definition: the oily substance in bodies and food
senses.example: Too much fat is not healthy.
senses.why: Old English fætt meant 'fattened, well fed'; the noun took the name of the substance that makes a body fat.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fætt 意为「养肥的、吃得好的」；名词就用这个词来指让身体变胖的那种物质。

senses.title: Having much body fat
senses.example: The cat is very fat.
senses.why: The adjective keeps the old sense of 'well fed': a body that has stored much fat is described as fat.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留了「养得肥」的旧义：储存了很多脂肪的身体就被形容为 fat。

senses.title: Containing much fat
senses.example: He likes fat pork.
senses.why: The same adjective is used of food that carries a lot of fat, because the meat itself is fattened.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也用于脂肪含量高的食物，因为那块肉本身就被养肥了。

definition_en: the person or thing liked best, or liked best of all
core_image: 孩子把最喜欢的绘本放在枕边，书角已经翻旧
scene: 孩子把最喜欢的绘本放在枕边，书角已经翻旧。This book is my favourite.
sceneCN: 这里 favourite 是「最喜欢的人或物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这本书是我的最爱。

senses.title: The one liked best
senses.definition: the person or thing one likes best
senses.example: This book is my favourite.
senses.why: Favourite comes from favour, 'to like or prefer'; the noun names the one thing that holds first place in your favour.
senses.whyCN: favourite 来自 favour「喜爱、偏爱」；这个名词指在你心里占第一位的那个。

senses.title: Liked best of all
senses.example: Blue is her favourite colour.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝色是她最喜欢的颜色。
senses.why: The adjective uses the same 'held in highest favour' idea before a noun, so it marks the top choice in a set.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把同一个「最受偏爱」的意思放在名词前，用来标记一组里的首选。

senses.title: A favoured person
senses.example: The teacher's favourite got the prize.
senses.exampleCN: 老师偏爱的学生得了奖。
senses.why: Because favour can be given unfairly, the noun also names a person singled out for special treatment, sometimes with a hint of disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 因为偏爱可能不公平，这个名词也指被特别照顾的人，有时带一点不以为然的意味。

definition_zh: 砍伐；打倒；掉下（fall 的过去式）
definition_en: to cut down a tree, to knock someone down, or the past tense of fall
core_image: 伐木工人挥斧砍向树干，木屑飞溅
scene: 伐木工人挥斧砍向树干，木屑飞溅。They will fell the old tree tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 fell 是「砍伐」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们明天要砍倒那棵老树。

senses.title: To cut down
senses.example: They will fell the old tree tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 他们明天要砍倒那棵老树。
senses.why: Fell as 'cut down' is a separate Old English verb fellan, 'make fall'; felling a tree means causing it to fall.
senses.whyCN: 表示砍伐的 fell 是另一个古英语动词 fellan「使倒下」；felling a tree 就是让树倒下来。

senses.title: To knock down
senses.example: The boxer felled his opponent with one punch.
senses.why: The same causative idea applies to people: to fell someone is to make that person go down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「使倒下」的意思也用在人身上：to fell someone 就是让那个人倒下。

senses.title: The past of fall
senses.definitionCN: fall 的过去式，表示掉了下去
senses.example: He fell off the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他从自行车上摔了下来。
senses.why: Old English feoll was the past form of feallan 'fall', and it survived unchanged in shape beside the separate verb fellan.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 feoll 是 feallan「落下」的过去式，它的形状原样保留下来，与另一个动词 fellan 同时存在。
